citations.title: Reliefs the District Commission can order

draft.body_markdown:
BEFORE THE DISTRICT CONSUMER DISPUTES REDRESSAL COMMISSION, JAIPUR

COMPLAINANT:
[[FILL: Your Full Name]]
[[FILL: Your Full Address]]
[[FILL: Your Phone Number]]
[[FILL: Your Email Address]]

VERSUS

OPPOSITE PARTY:
[[FILL: Name of E-commerce Company]]
[[FILL: Registered Office Address of the Company]]

COMPLAINT UNDER SECTION 35 OF THE CONSUMER PROTECTION ACT, 2019

MOST RESPECTFULLY SHOWETH:

1. I am a consumer as defined under Section 2(7) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, having purchased a phone for Rs 18,499 from the Opposite Party's online platform (Order ID: OD12345).

2. The product was found to be unsatisfactory, and I initiated a return request. The Opposite Party successfully completed the pickup of the returned phone on 10 September 2026.

3. Despite the successful return of the product, the Opposite Party has failed to process the refund of Rs 18,499. 

4. I have made multiple attempts to resolve this issue with the Opposite Party, raising 4 separate grievance tickets, the last of which was raised on 01 October 2026. The Opposite Party continues to state that the refund is 'under process' without providing a concrete timeline or resolution.

5. The failure to refund the amount for a returned product constitutes a 'deficiency in service' under Section 2(11) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, as the Opposite Party has failed to adhere to the reasonable timelines for refunds as required by law.

6. This Commission has the pecuniary jurisdiction to entertain this complaint as the value of the goods is Rs 18,499, which is well within the limit of the District Commission. This Commission also has territorial jurisdiction as I reside in Jaipur and the cause of action arose here.

7. The complaint is filed within the limitation period of two years as prescribed under Section 69 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

RELIEFS PRAYED:
In view of the facts stated above, it is prayed that this Hon'ble Commission may be pleased to direct the Opposite Party to:

a) Refund the amount of Rs 18,499 immediately along with interest at the rate of 12% per annum from the date of pickup (10 September 2026) until the date of actual payment.

b) Pay a sum of Rs [[FILL: Amount]] as compensation for the mental agony and harassment caused by the deficiency in service.

c) Pay a sum of Rs [[FILL: Amount]] towards the cost of litigation.

LIST OF DOCUMENTS ANNEXED:
1. Copy of Order ID OD12345.
2. [[FILL: Copy of any communication/emails/screenshots of ticket history]].

VERIFICATION:
I, [[FILL: Your Full Name]], the Complainant, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to 7 are true to my personal knowledge and belief. No part of it is false and nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at Jaipur on this [[FILL: Date]] day of [[FILL: Month]], 2026.

_____________________
(Signature of Complainant)

citations.title: Who is a 'consumer'
citations.plain: You are a consumer if you buy goods or hire/avail a service for payment (paid, promised, or in instalments), including online, teleshopping, direct selling or multi-level marketing. People who use the goods or service with the buyer's approval are also covered. Buying for resale or a commercial purpose is excluded, but buying something to earn your own livelihood through self-employment is not treated as commercial.

citations.title: Meaning of 'deficiency' in service
citations.plain: A deficiency is any fault, shortcoming or inadequacy in the quality, nature or manner of a service that the law or a contract requires. It also covers negligence or acts or omissions that cause you loss, and deliberately withholding relevant information from you.

citations.title: Who can file a complaint, and electronic filing
citations.plain: A complaint can be filed with the District Commission by the consumer, by a registered consumer association, by one or more consumers on behalf of many with the same interest (with the Commission's permission), or by the Central/State Government or the Central Authority. The Act allows complaints to be filed electronically, and the prescribed fee can be paid electronically.

citations.title: Limitation period for filing complaint
citations.plain: You must file a consumer complaint within two years from the date the problem (cause of action) arose. A later complaint can still be accepted if you show sufficient cause for the delay, but the Commission must record its reasons for condoning the delay.

citations.act: Consumer Protection (Jurisdiction of the District Commission, the State Commission and the National Commission) Rules, 2021
citations.title: Money limits of District, State and National Commissions
citations.plain: Where you file depends on how much you paid for the goods or service. Up to Rs 50 lakh: District Commission. Above Rs 50 lakh and up to Rs 2 crore: State Commission. Above Rs 2 crore: National Commission (NCDRC).

citations.title: E-commerce refunds must be paid within a reasonable time
citations.plain: Once a refund request is accepted, the platform must pay it within a reasonable time, or within the time set by RBI or other applicable law. The rules do not fix a specific number of days.

citations.title: Seller/platform cannot refuse return or refund for defective, deficient, spurious or late goods
citations.plain: A seller on a marketplace (rule 6(3)) and an inventory e-commerce entity (rule 7(4)) cannot refuse to take back goods or refuse a refund if the goods or services are defective, deficient or spurious, or not as advertised. The same applies if delivery was late, unless the delay was due to force majeure.

send_instructions: Visit the e-Jagriti portal (https://e-jagriti.gov.in/) to register and create an account.
Fill in the details of the Opposite Party (the company) using their official registered office address (usually found on their website's 'Contact Us' or 'Legal' page).
Upload a PDF copy of this complaint, signed by you, along with copies of your Order ID and any screenshots of your ticket history.
Since the claim amount is below Rs 5 lakh, there is no filing fee required.
Submit the complaint online and save the acknowledgement receipt provided by the portal.
Keep a digital copy of all submitted documents and the acknowledgement for your records.
